intro_notes: NOTE: Requirements in this merit badge are to be completed using a manually-powered cycle. Use of electric or hybrid-electric bikes is not permitted. Check out the Digital Resource Guide for the Cycling merit badge HERE for information and helpful resources to engage your learning and assist you along on your merit badge journey! The official merit badge pamphlets are now free and downloadable HERE or can be purchased at the Scout Shop.

requirements.req_text: Do the following: (a) Explain to your counselor the most likely hazards you may encounter while participating in cycling activities and what you should do to anticipate, help prevent, mitigate, and respond to these hazards. Explain to your counselor how to ride predictably, be conspicuous, think ahead, and ride ready. (b) Show that you know first aid for injuries or illnesses that could occur while cycling, including cuts, scratches, concussions, blisters, sunburn, heat exhaustion, heatstroke, hypothermia, frostbite, dehydration, insect stings, tick bites, and snakebite. Explain to your counselor why you should be able to identify the poisonous plants and poisonous animals that are found in your area.

pamphlet_excerpts: Wash Cuts Scratches: Wash cuts, scratches, and scrapes with soap and water.
Cover Larger Wounds: Cover larger wounds with a sterile gauzepad or a clean cloth folded into a pad.
Sunburn Cause Lasting: Sunburn can cause lasting skin damage and the potential for skin cancer.
Cover Prevent Sunburn: Cover up to prevent sunburn, and use plenty of sunscreen with a sun protection factor (SPF) of at least 15.
step_by_step_procedure: Toease Pain Mild: Toease the pain of a mild sunburn, apply cool, wet cloths to the affected area.
Soothing Lotion Containing: A soothing lotion containing chamomile or aloe vera may provide relief.
Concussion Brain Injury: A concussion is a brain injury, caused by a blow to the heador by a sudden change in motion of the head, in which thebrain bounces rapidly back.
Aperson Does Not: Aperson does not need to be knocked out to have a concussion.

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: Before departing on a 25-mile troop road ride, you check a Scout's helmet and notice the front rim sits high on the forehead (4 fingers above the eyebrows) and the side straps form a loose loop below the chin. How must the helmet be adjusted?
options: Tilt the helmet back further so the Scout can see traffic lights more easily.

Apply the 2-V-1 helmet fit rule: level the rim 1 to 2 finger-widths above the eyebrows, adjust side sliders to form a snug 'V' right under each ear, and tighten the chin buckle until only 1 finger fits underneath.
Wear a thick winter beanie underneath the loose straps without tightening the retention dial.
quiz_item.correct_answer: Option B — Level the helmet 1-2 fingers above the eyebrows, form a 'V' under the ears, and snug the chin strap to 1 finger width.
quiz_item.explanation: A helmet tilted back exposes the frontal skull in a forward crash; the BSA Cycling Pamphlet's 2-V-1 fit check keeps the helmet level and secure during impact.

pamphlet_excerpts: However Not Delay: However, you should not delay faster driversunnecessarily.
Going Same Speed: If you are going the same speed as other vehicles, pull intoline with them.
Don Ride Too: Don’t ride too close to the vehicle you arepassing.
Return Right Lane: After you pass, return to the right lane as soon asis convenient.
step_by_step_procedure: Intersection Point Driveway: An intersection is any point, including a driveway, where thepaths of two vehicles can cross.
There Ways Throughan: There are ways to get throughan intersection as easily and safely as possible.
Move Lane Position: First, always move to the lane position that will allow you toride through most efficiently.
Right Side Straight: To turn right, get to the right side; to go straight, stay near the middle; to turn left, move just to theright of the center of the roadway.

pamphlet_excerpts: America Bike Safety: The Scouting America Bike Safety Guidelines are designed to make bicycle ridingsafer and more enjoyable for you and others.
Review Guidelines Your merit: Review these guidelines with your merit badge counselor.
Activities Principlesshould: As with all Scouting activities, these principlesshould be applied in your cycling event.
Bicycle Helmetscan Reduce: Bicycle helmetscan reduce head injuries by 85 percent, according to the NHTSA.
step_by_step_procedure: Stand Top Tube: Make sure you can stand over the top tube of your bicycle.
Assurethat Tires Fully: Assurethat tires are fully inflated and brakes are working properly.
Wear Clothing Visible: Wear clothing that makes you more visible, such as bright neonor fluorescent colors.
Lookout Hazards Potholes: Be on the lookout for hazards, such as potholes, broken glass, gravel, puddles, leaves, animals, or anything thatcould cause you to crash.

requirements.req_text: Using a bicycle safety checklist, clean and adjust a bicycle and present it to your counselor for inspection. Do the following: (a) Show points that should be checked regularly to make sure the bicycle is safe to ride. (b) Show how to adjust the saddle and handlebars for a proper fit. (c) Show how to adjust brakes and gear shifting (derailleurs). (d) Show all points that need regular lubrication. (e) Show how to repair a flat by removing the tire, replacing or patching the tube, and remounting the tire. (f) Show that the bicycle meets local laws.

pamphlet_excerpts: Engage Brakes Prevent: To mount the bicycle, engage the brakes to prevent the bike fromrolling.
Swing Leg Bike: Swing either leg up and over the bike and straddle thetop tube.
Foot Toturn Crank: Use your foot toturn the crank backward until it reaches the 10 o’clock position.
Your body Moves Bike: As your body moves up and the bike moves forward, the saddle willmove under you.
step_by_step_procedure: Opposite Pedal Reaches: When the opposite pedal reaches the 12 o’clockposition, make a second pedal stroke.
Dismount Left Pedal: To dismount, place the left pedal straight down and standon it like a step.
Bike Come Stop: As the bike is about to come to a stop, lean alittle to the right and put your right foot on the ground.
Soonas Position Left: As soonas you can, position the left pedal to the 10 o’clock position inpreparation for starting again.

requirements.lead_text: Using the Scouting America buddy system, complete all of the requirements for ONE of the following options: Road Biking OR Trail or Mixed Surface Biking. Resource: The Buddy System in Scouting: Why No Scout Should Go It Alone (website)
requirements.req_text: Using the Scouting America buddy system, complete all of the requirements for ONE of the following options: Road Biking OR Trail or Mixed Surface Biking. Resource: The Buddy System in Scouting: Why No Scout Should Go It Alone (website) (a) Option A—Road Biking. Do ALL of the following: (1) Take a road safety test with your counselor and demonstrate the following: (a) On an urban street with light traffic, properly execute a left turn from the center of the street; also demonstrate an alternate left-turn technique used during periods of heavy traffic. (b) Properly execute a right turn. (c) Demonstrate appropriate actions at a right-turn-only lane when you are continuing straight. (d) Show proper curbside and road-edge riding. Show how to ride safely along a row of parked cars. (e) Cross railroad tracks properly. (2) Avoiding main highways, take two rides of 10 miles each, two rides of 15 miles each, and two rides of 25 miles each. You must make a report of the rides taken. List dates for the routes traveled, and interesting things seen on the ride. (3) After completing requirement (2) for the road biking option, do ONE of the following: (a) Lay out on a road map a 50-mile trip. Stay away from main highways. Using your map, make this ride in eight hours or less. (b) Participate in an organized bike tour of at least 50 miles. Make this ride in eight hours or less. Afterward, use the tour's cue sheet to make a map of the ride. (b) Option B—Trail or Mixed Surface Biking. Do ALL of the following: Note: These requirements may be completed using a mountain bike or other properly equipped, manually-powered cycle such as a gravel bike, tandem bike, hand-powered bike, recumbent bike, adult tricycle, or adaptive cycle. If a tandem bike is used, the Scout must actively power the cycle in concert with the other rider. (1) Demonstrate the following mountain bike handling skills to your counselor: (a) Neutral position, ready position, bike body separation (side to side, and forward and back), and body positioning for cornering (b) Show shifting skills as applicable to climbs and obstacles. (c) Show proper technique for riding up and down hills, including when you would ride seated, crouched, or standing. (2) Take a trail safety test with your counselor and demonstrate the following: (a) Show proper trail etiquette to hikers and other cyclists, including when to yield the right-of-way. Resource: Bike Trail Etiquette (video) (b) Demonstrate how to correctly cross an obstacle by either going over the obstacle on your bike or dismounting your bike and crossing over or around the obstacle. (c) Cross rocks, gravel, and roots properly (3) Describe the rules of trail riding, including how to know when a trail is unsuitable for riding. (4) On mountain biking or multi-use trails approved by your counselor, take two rides of 2 miles each, two rides of 5 miles each, and two rides of 8 miles each. You must make a report of the rides taken. List dates for the routes traveled, and interesting things seen. (5) After fulfilling the previous requirement, lay out on a trail map a 22-mile trip. You may include multiple trail systems, if needed. Stay away from main highways. Using your map, complete this ride in one day.

sub_requirements.sub_req_text: Option B—Trail or Mixed Surface Biking. Do ALL of the following: Note: These requirements may be completed using a mountain bike or other properly equipped, manually-powered cycle such as a gravel bike, tandem bike, hand-powered bike, recumbent bike, adult tricycle, or adaptive cycle. If a tandem bike is used, the Scout must actively power the cycle in concert with the other rider. (1) Demonstrate the following mountain bike handling skills to your counselor: (a) Neutral position, ready position, bike body separation (side to side, and forward and back), and body positioning for cornering (b) Show shifting skills as applicable to climbs and obstacles. (c) Show proper technique for riding up and down hills, including when you would ride seated, crouched, or standing. (2) Take a trail safety test with your counselor and demonstrate the following: (a) Show proper trail etiquette to hikers and other cyclists, including when to yield the right-of-way. Resource: Bike Trail Etiquette (video) (b) Demonstrate how to correctly cross an obstacle by either going over the obstacle on your bike or dismounting your bike and crossing over or around the obstacle. (c) Cross rocks, gravel, and roots properly (3) Describe the rules of trail riding, including how to know when a trail is unsuitable for riding. (4) On mountain biking or multi-use trails approved by your counselor, take two rides of 2 miles each, two rides of 5 miles each, and two rides of 8 miles each. You must make a report of the rides taken. List dates for the routes traveled, and interesting things seen. (5) After fulfilling the previous requirement, lay out on a trail map a 22-mile trip. You may include multiple trail systems, if needed. Stay away from main highways. Using your map, complete this ride in one day.

pamphlet_excerpts: Side-to-side Bike Body: Using side-to-side bike/body separation, you can control your bike through many tight turns on trails.
Practice Skill Relatively: Practice this skill on a relatively flat space with some markers (cones, half tennisballs, or rocks and sticks) and mark out a 90-degree turn.
Practice Riding Turns: Practice riding through the turns several times, increasing your speed, off the saddle and with level pedals.
Pushyour Bike Turn: Pushyour bike into the turn, keep your head up and look at your exitpoint, one finger on each brake lever.
step_by_step_procedure: Steep Climbs Rider: On steep climbs a rider may choose one of three positions: seated, crouched, or standing.
Seated Position Rider: In the seated position, the rider’sshoulders move forward and the rider may move forward on thesaddle.
Terrain Becomes Steeper: As the terrain becomes steeper, a rider may need to moveinto a crouched position similar to a ready position.
Positionprovides Power Bike: This positionprovides more power, bike/body separation, and better tractioncontrol.
